rubric: The workshop title is clearly the dominant element and is much larger than every other piece of text.
The date, time and place are easy to find, grouped together, and use no more than about three levels of emphasis overall.
Lines are set comfortably: sensible line length and line-height, no awkward one-word last lines, and no clipped or cramped text.
The card uses a small, consistent set of type styles (one or two families, few sizes and weights) with consistent alignment.
All text, including the smallest line, has strong contrast and is readable at phone size.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both cards make the title the largest text, but in each it is only about twice the size of the date. A keeps the date, time, place and what-to-bring together in one card with consistent type, and every line is dark enough to read. B puts the date and location in two separate wide boxes and uses more text sizes, from the very small DATE & TIME and LOCATION labels and 'Learn more:' up to the title. B's sign-up URL is light tan on cream and the button text is white on light tan, both weak in contrast, while A's dark URL is small but readable. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both cards make the title clearly dominant and group the event details well, but B puts date, time, location and what to bring in one card, which is tighter and easier to scan. A's most important action line, the URL, is light tan on cream, and its white-on-tan button is also low contrast; A also leaves a large empty gap above the button. B's URL is small and italic, and its grey labels are a bit light, but its text reads better overall at phone size.
